Article Title: Meet Aditi Paudel, a 17-year-old high school student appointed as Japan's first literacy ambassador
Article Text: Born in Japan, and raised in Nepal during her early childhood, Aditi Paudel had always shown an affinity towards reading. Her earliest memory of reading is of her grandfather handing her a newspaper filled with intricate Devanagari script when she was still in preschool. But to the surprise of those around her, she was still able to make sense of the text. Over the years, she has only improved and the now 17-year-old high school senior in Tokyo was recently appointed as Japan's first literacy ambassador, as per a report by The Japan Times.The World Literacy Foundation, a global nonprofit headquartered in Australia is running a program where around 900 young people between the ages of 16 and 25 from 101 countries are participating. While the program has been running for 12 years, this is the first time an ambassador from Japan has been appointed, according to Andrew Kay, CEO and founder of the World Literacy Foundation.The aim of the program is to connect young people around the world and get them “involved and waving the flag for literacy in their community,” Kay said, noting that Paudel was singled out “for her leadership, passion for literacy, and commitment to empowering young people in Japan.”“Her curiosity about English shaped thoughtful advocacy, strengthening the program’s global voice and cultural reach,” he added.Paudel returned to Japan to enter the third grade and along with settling into a new life, she found herself having to learn Japanese once more, which meant turning to the books. Her love for reading came pretty early in her life, nurtured by her father who bought her plenty of books. She developed an early taste for fantasy, and recalled falling in love with Enid Blyton’s “The Wishing-Chair.”Reading Malala Yousafzai 's autobiography, 'I Am Malala', helped her develop significant interests in female empowerment, including ensuring that women across the world have access to education and literacy. Along with working with children with disabilities, she plans to work with the Shanti Volunteer Association to collect and donate books to Asian countries with lower rates of literacy, including Nepal.With enough experience developing her own reading skills, Paudel said that a common view of literacy is how well a person can read or write, but she sees it in broader terms. Essentially, it’s “something that helps you open doors for more opportunities,” she noted.Paudel has experienced the impact of her access to private education firsthand and how it has set her life on a different course. “My parents grew up in a completely opposite environment. They did not have a childhood like this,” she said. “Being literate is so important because even though you have the potential, you can never unlock it if you do not have literacy.”But even those with easy access to books are reading less than they once did. Around half of elementary, junior high and high school age children in Japan do not read books, according to a recent study by Benesse Educational Research & Development Institute and the University of Tokyo.Fewer young people are reading for pleasure and enjoyment, said Kay, and that could cause a significant regressive effect. “As far as embedding themselves in a novel or reading something that really takes a little bit more effort, that is becoming a rarer thing,” he said. Kay also cautions against the impact of artificial intelligence, noting that the latest tech tools provide quick answers, allowing people to skip the process of researching, reading and wrestling with theories and thoughts oneself.“It’s turning our clock back 150 years … where most people couldn’t read or would have limited ability to read,” he said of the absence of reading books as a mainstream pursuit. Those trends only add importance to initiatives like the World Literacy Foundation’s ambassador program.As a teenager, Paudel understands growing up in a world full of distractions, where much of life is on and from social media. “You will always be more inclined to go for your phone rather than a book,” she said, and because of this, making reading a habit is critical. Her advice for developing a love of reading isn’t about ticking classics off a book list, but finding something that resonates, and that, ideally, can broaden the reader’s perspective.
Article Summary: Aditi paudel, a 17-year-old high school senior in tokyo, was recently appointed as japan's first literacy ambassador. The world literacy foundation is running a program where around 900 young people between the ages of 16 and 25 from 101 countries are participating. This is the first time an ambassador from japan has been appointed.

Article Title: Translating the Reliance ethos into a blueprint for nation-building
Article Text:
Translating familial empathy into enterprise resilience

Democratising technology for a billion aspirations

Reclaiming soft power and passing the baton

There is a prevailing wisdom in global business schools that suggests the larger an enterprise grows, the colder it must become. Scale, the theory goes, demands a clinical detachment. Yet, in the heart of India's corporate landscape, a remarkably different experiment has been playing out for decades. Here, the traditional Indian family ethos has not been discarded as an archaic social structure but rather leveraged as a sophisticated business strategy.The recently released Reliance documentary, 'Parvah Hai Toh Parivar Hai', pulls back the curtain on this machinery. It offers a case study of what happens when the ethics of a household extend to a conglomerate employing hundreds of thousands, and ultimately to a nation of 1.4 billion people.Stripping away the complex financial jargon often associated with India's largest enterprise, the film reveals a foundational philosophy rooted in care, trust, and self-reliance. It asks a compelling question: can familial empathy actually drive a nation's socio-economic trajectory?At the corporate level, this paternalistic model is far more than a warm metaphor. It operates as a highly effective structural framework. The fundamental premise that care defines a family dictates how the company handles its human capital. During moments of intense crisis, such as health emergencies or natural disasters, this responsibility translates into the swift mobilisation of healthcare, isolation facilities, and emergency resources.This culture of protective support builds a rare institutional resilience, fostering a fiercely loyal ecosystem. Recalling the early days of setting up Jio Studios, an executive describes the deep personal involvement of the leadership. "I remember Mukesh Bhai and Manoj Bhai laying out their vision for the media business," she notes. "I remember thinking, do I have to pay to work here because this kind of mentorship is something that money cannot buy. "When creative and professional ventures face unexpected headwinds, this cushion of corporate confidence remains largely intact. Actor Ranveer Singh, reflecting on his collaborations with the conglomerate, highlighted this unusual patience. "I was given all the love, all the support and all the encouragement even at a time when my movies were not doing well," he shares in the film. "Career ups and downs. But to have received that kind of support meant a lot to me. It's nothing short of a blessing, an honour and a privilege to be associated with the Ambani family."However, the true test of any family-led business model lies in its ability to step outside its own perimeter and serve the wider community. For Reliance, modern nation building has meant translating massive corporate capacity into accessible public utility. Having already rewired India's digital landscape by making high-speed data universal through Jio, the enterprise is now looking towards the next frontier.The leadership frequently questions how their scale affects the masses. According to the documentary, the next step involves using new age technologies to bridge socio-economic gaps. "How does it affect the 1.4 billion people of India as we democratise information," the film asks, noting that generative artificial intelligence is "now democratising intelligence amongst 1.4 billion people."The ambition is to create tools that serve every stratum of society. The narrative paints a stark rural reality, envisioning a person in Bhagalpur "able to really use an AI tutor to teach himself or a farmer who is able to really understand what his food productivity would be." As the leadership points out, with this knowledge, "he is able to think more, he is able to do more, he is able to earn more and that is I think the ultimate goal for us. "Recognising that there are many Indias cutting across different income classes, the company is pivoting toward voice-first interfaces designed for the country's vast linguistic diversity. The documentary rightly points out that "Indians actually converse with technology by voice first rather than text." It is framed as a massive opportunity "which truly only an Indian company can solve." This ethos of mass accessibility comes directly from the top. As Mukesh Ambani directed his team regarding their massive streaming footprint: "The business is always important but I want consumers to experience our innovation."Beyond digital infrastructure, nation building requires fierce cultural stewardship. This household-led framework views corporate success as a catalyst for preserving national identity. Noting that foreign companies have historically dominated the sector, the documentary asserts, "There was no reason why an Indian company should not be leading the charts on media."Through Jio Studios, the mandate is bold: "What we want to do is claim back the narrative of India, especially young India." By backing massive commercial cinema alongside globally recognised projects, the conglomerate is actively shaping India's cultural footprint. Furthermore, spaces like the Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre serve a dual purpose. "The vision of Mrs. Ambani and the vision of our centre is bringing the best of the world to India and the best of India to the world," the film notes.As the company approaches its 50th year, it stands at a critical juncture. Mukesh Ambani frames this generational shift not as a standard corporate handover, but as a continuation of core values. "Akash, Isha and Anant are only representatives of the young leaders," he explains. "And they will take our values. They will build an India of our dreams."At its heart, the enterprise remains anchored by its dining table roots. "To me, family is everything. I feel privileged that four generations of our family live together," shares Nita Ambani. This restless drive is perhaps best captured by 88-year-old V. Balasubramanian, who has spent 62 years at Reliance. He shares, "When I go away from this world, Dhirubhai is waiting there. We will start another Reliance Industries there and start working there and building up another empire. "Ultimately, the Reliance narrative suggests that India's economic rise is deeply intertwined with business models that align commercial scale with societal care. By treating a nation as an extended family, the company offers a compelling, distinctly Indian blueprint for modern nation building.
Article Summary: Reliance documentary 'parvah hai toh parivar hai' offers a case study of what happens when the ethics of a household extend to a conglomerate employing hundreds of thousands. For reliance, modern nation building has meant translating massive corporate capacity into accessible public utility.

Article Title: The Rs 2.05 crore question: Can Meta be blamed for what its glasses record?
Article Text:
Secretly filmed by Meta glasses: Why a Delhi man is demanding Rs 2.05 crore (Reuters image)

So, what allegedly happened?

Why has Meta been named?

What Meta says about safeguards against covert recording

What studies have found about privacy and camera-equipped glasses

What the legal notice demands from Meta and the Instagram creator

A Delhi man has sent a legal notice to an Instagram creator and Meta Platforms after he was allegedly harassed and covertly filmed at a café using Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses.The footage was subsequently posted on Instagram and viewed more than 4.19 lakh times.He has demanded that the video be removed, an apology issued and ₹2.05 crore paid in damages.But the notice, issued on August 24, goes beyond the actions of the creator. It seeks to hold Meta responsible in two capacities: as the owner of Instagram, which allegedly continued to host the reel after receiving complaints, and as the technology company behind the design and marketing of the camera-equipped glasses used to record it.The Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF), which provided the victim pro bono legal assistance, says this is, to its knowledge, among the first legal actions in India to directly raise the liability of a smart-glasses maker for harm allegedly enabled by its product design.The case has not been decided by a court yet and the claims in the notice, so far, remain allegations. The man, whose identity has been withheld and who is referred to as X, is represented by advocate Apar Gupta.According to IFF, X was sitting alone at a Costa Coffee outlet in Delhi’s Khan Market on July 24 when a stranger, who eventually turned out to be a creator, approached him.The creator allegedly pestered and insulted him with unsolicited questions and remarks and followed him inside the café. X complained to the staff and eventually moved to another seating area to get away from the unpleasant situation thrust upon him.What he did not know, IFF says, was that the encounter was allegedly being recorded through Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses. One or more of the creator’s associates also allegedly filmed the exchange from other angles without his knowledge or consent.The footage was posted as an Instagram reel on July 26. By August 6, according to IFF, it had received more than 4.19 lakh views, approximately 15,700 likes and over 500 comments.X reported both the video and the account to Instagram on July 27. According to IFF, the reporting menu offered no category specifically covering invasion of privacy or non-consensual recording. The victim, therefore, selected “bullying or harassment”.He also submitted a separate complaint to Meta’s grievance officer for India under “Privacy violation — sharing of personal information or representation without consent.”Instagram subsequently informed him that the reported material doesn’t go against its “Community Standards”, according to IFF.The most significant part of the notice concerns the glasses themselves.Developed by Meta in partnership with eyewear company EssilorLuxottica, Ray-Ban Meta glasses resemble conventional eyewear but allow users to take photographs and record videos hands-free. They were launched in India in May 2025 at a starting price of ₹29,900.The glasses have a small white capture LED on the front that indicates when the camera is being used. The notice argues that this warning is inadequate because it can easily be missed by someone who does not know that the glasses contain a camera.“The recording indicator on the said devices is inadequate and easily overlooked, and the harm that eventuated to our client is due to a design that is foreseeably enabled,” the notice states.It argues that Meta “owed and breached a duty of care” to X and was negligent in contributing to the alleged intrusion into his privacy.Crucially, the notice argues that this liability arises from Meta’s own product-design and marketing decisions and is therefore separate from its role as an online intermediary.Section 79 of the Information Technology Act provides conditional protection to online intermediaries against liability for content posted by third parties. The notice contends that such protection cannot extend to a negligence claim arising from Meta’s own product design.That argument has not yet been tested in court.The Delhi dispute could now test a different question: whether a company that makes wearable cameras has a responsibility not merely to indicate that recording is taking place, but to ensure that an unsuspecting bystander can reasonably understand that they are being filmed.To know more, subscribe and read the full story on TOI+ — Secretly filmed by Meta glasses: Why a Delhi man is demanding Rs 2.05 crore
Article Summary: A delhi man has sent a legal notice to an instagram creator and meta platforms. He was allegedly harassed and covertly filmed at a café using ray-ban meta smart glasses. The footage was subsequently posted on instagram and viewed more than 4.19 lakh times. He has demanded that the video be removed, an apology issued and rs 2.05 crore paid in damages.

Article Title: Indian consulate in UAE issues warning over biometric fraud targeting nationals
Article Text:
The advisory urged nationals not to share their passports, Emirates IDs, biometric data, including eye, face or fingerprint scans, or personal and financial credentials with unauthorised individuals or agencies under any circumstances.

NEW DELHI: The consulate general of India in Dubai has warned Indian nationals in the UAE, particularly blue-collar workers, against handing over biometric data. The warning advised the workers against unauthorised agents claiming to help with visa regularisation, Emergency Certificates, Exit Permits, Emirates IDs or employment, after reports of fraud involving the misuse of fingerprints and facial scans.In an advisory issued on Monday, the consulate said it had received information about individuals and agents allegedly exploiting Indians seeking assistance with immigration and documentation procedures. The fraudsters reportedly ask victims to provide fingerprints or face scans, which can then be used without their knowledge to conduct financial transactions, open bank accounts or obtain loans and credit cards in their names.The consulate cautioned that such misuse could leave victims liable for financial obligations or transactions they did not authorise. In some cases, those affected could also face multiple fines, travel bans and even imprisonment.The advisory urged nationals not to share their passports, Emirates IDs, biometric data, including eye, face or fingerprint scans, or personal and financial credentials with unauthorised individuals or agencies under any circumstances.It also clarified that biometric information required for procedures such as exit permits, Emirates IDs or visa regularisation must be provided only at official UAE Government facilities or counters. People were specifically warned against submitting such information through private individuals, agents or third-party service providers claiming to be authorised by UAE authorities.The consulate also sought to dispel a potential source of confusion by stating that biometric information is not required for certain consular services.The advisory said the Consulate General of India in Dubai and the Embassy of India in Abu Dhabi "DO NOT require any fingerprint scan or face/eye scan from applicants for the issuance of a passport or emergency certificate."It warned that any person or agent demanding such information while claiming to represent the Indian Embassy or consulate would be engaging in fraudulent activity and should not be entertained.Indians approached by unauthorised individuals seeking biometric data or Emirates IDs have been advised to contact the Pravasi Bharatiya Sahayata Kendra through the toll-free number 80046342, WhatsApp or SMS at 00971543090571, or email pbsk.dubai@mea.gov.in to verify credentials or seek assistance.The consulate urged Indian nationals living in or visiting the UAE to exercise caution, independently verify the credentials of anyone offering immigration or documentation-related services, and report suspicious activity to the Indian consulate and the relevant UAE authorities.
Article Summary: The consulate general of india in dubai has warned indian nationals in the uae, particularly blue-collar workers, against handing over biometric data. The warning advised the workers against unauthorised agents claiming to help with visa regularisation, emergency certificates, exit permits, emirates ids or employment.

Article Title: Year-wise plan to implement Samudra Manthan in works
Article Text:
Petroleum minister Hardeep Puri reviewed the action taken on decisions from two brainstorming sessions on the rollout of the scheme, which received Cabinet’s approval, said officials. (Photo: IANS)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Government is likely to finalise a year-wise plan soon for drilling, seismic surveys and rig deployment under Samudra Manthan, a Rs 84,084-crore national programme aimed at stepping up oil and gas exploration in India’s offshore basins and reducing dependence on energy imports.Officials said petroleum minister Hardeep Puri recently reviewed the action taken on decisions from two brainstorming sessions held in Gurgaon in Haryana and Duliajan in Assam, on the rollout of the scheme, which received Cabinet’s approval last month.The year-wise roadmap will help government carry out exploration and production activities in a concerted manner across Krishna-Godavari (KG), Mahanadi, Andaman and Cauvery basins and ensure systematic utilisation of funds, an official said.The scheme will fund acquisition, processing and interpretation of seismic data, scientific drilling in frontier basins, accelerated exploration in deepwater and ultra-deepwater blocks, and development of shared offshore production and evacuation infrastructure.While Rs 43,200 crore has been earmarked for drilling 60 exploratory deepwater wells over five years, Rs 28,534 crore has been allocated for acquisition of 2D and 3D seismic data, Rs 10,000 crore for common infrastructure hubs and Rs 2,000 crore for an oil and gas manufacturing and services zone.India’s annual crude oil requirement is around 256 million tonnes (MT), of which nearly 88 per cent is imported. Domestic crude oil production from 26 sedimentary basins is estimated at around 28 MT. With domestic output stagnating even as demand continues to rise, government has been looking to step up exploration to improve energy security and reduce import dependence.Samudra Manthan is expected to add more than 600 million metric tonnes of oil equivalent (MMTOE) to the country’s hydrocarbon reserves and boost domestic production of crude oil and natural gas.Officials said government has implemented a series of upstream sector reforms over the past decade, including opening up almost the entire offshore acreage for exploration, changes to legal and contractual framework, and strengthening National Data Repository. Samudra Manthan would complement these reforms by providing public funding for offshore exploration and facilitating the deployment of advanced technologies, they said.The scheme also includes dedicated provisions for digital programme management, capacity building, technology adoption, stakeholder engagement and international outreach, creating an integrated ecosystem to accelerate offshore exploration and production in the country.
Article Summary: Samudra manthan is a rs 84,084-crore national programme aimed at stepping up oil and gas exploration in india’s offshore basins. The scheme will fund acquisition, processing and interpretation of seismic data, scientific drilling in frontier basins, accelerated exploration in deepwater and ultra-deepwater blocks.

Article Title: Wireless communication picked up; search operation launched in J&K's Samba
Article Text:
The hilly area of Sumb is considered strategically important from a security perspective. (PTI photo)

JAMMU: Security forces launched a joint search operation in the remote, hilly hamlet of Sumb in J&K’s Samba district after receiving information that a wireless set had been briefly activated in the area and satellite communication was detected around 1pm Tuesday.“The reported activation of Iridium satellite sets raised suspicion among security agencies, following which a combined team of the Army, police, and personnel from other forces rushed to Sumb’s Makoli village and initiated extensive searches in and around the area,” an official said Wednesday.“Terrorists often switch off such communication devices after contacting their handlers across the border,” said a source, adding that Iridium sets can be used on smartphones through the “Iridium GO!” mobile application, which creates a local Wi-Fi network that an iOS or Android phone can connect to.The operation continued until late Tuesday, but no satellite set or other suspicious material was found. Security was tightened along all routes leading to Sumb, with J&K Police and Village Defence Guards maintaining strict vigil, officials said.The hilly area of Sumb is considered strategically important from a security perspective as the route runs along the Basantar river and leads towards the India-Pakistan international border. Due to its proximity to the border, Samba district is a hotbed of terrorist activities. It serves as a gateway district for ultras heading towards Kashmir Valley via the upper reaches of Samba-Udhampur-Doda-Kishtwar.
Article Summary: Security forces launched a joint search operation in the remote, hilly hamlet of sumb in j&k’s samba district after receiving information that a wireless set had been briefly activated. The operation continued until late tuesday, but no satellite set or other suspicious material was found.

Article Title: Tom Brady's wealth skyrockets as his $500 million Las Vegas Raiders investment grows ahead of new season
Article Text:
Tom Brady's wealth.(Image via Getty Images)

Tom Brady’s wealth grows as his investment in the Las Vegas Raiders continues to increase its value ahead of the new season

Tom Brady makes it clear what he is focusing on ahead of the new season

Tom Brady, the seven time Super Bowl champion, was one of the greatest athletes in the world whose personal life has dominated headlines throughout his career. While Tom Brady is already a multi millionaire, it seems his wealth has increased more in the last few weeks.As per reports, Tom Brady’s investment in the Las Vegas Raiders has grown significantly in the last few weeks.As per Celebrity Net Worth, Tom Brady’s 5% share in the team is roughly worth a whopping $500 million since the Las Vegas Raiders is now valued at a whopping $10 billion.Back in October 2024, Tom Brady and Knighthead Capital Management co-founder Tom Wagner purchased a combined 10% stake in the Las Vegas Raiders for a whopping $220 million. Out of this, the NFL legend owns a 5% stake in the team.A few months ago, in an interview with CNBC, Tom Brady opened up about his stake in the Las Vegas Raiders as he said, “I’m a minority owner. So, when you’re that, there’s really no job description. I don’t really have a daily role…”The seven time Super Bowl champion added, “You know, my phone call is always available to everybody who needs it. I want to see everyone succeed, be their best, bring a winning kind of a culture to Las Vegas — to bring the Raiders back to glory.I’d love to be a part of it.”Back in August 2025, the Las Vegas Raiders' estimated value had already climbed to about $7.7 billion which again increased by May 2026.While Tom Brady has only gotten more and more wealthier in the last few years, his only focus has been his children.A few years ago, in an interview, Tom Brady opened up about fatherhood as he said, "I'm 44. I've got a family that I'm a dad to some amazing children…When I think about being a dad, I think about him because of what my dad meant to me, and I know I'm not as good a dad to my kids that my dad's been to me.”The star player added, “And I use them as my example as to how to keep a family together and to care and to support and to love."The seven time Super Bowl champion added, "We want our kids to be happy. I want them to be respectful of people. I want them to be kind. I wanna make the world a better place." However, he also expressed his hope that his children learn from his experience.

Article Title: India’s tech workforce gets another jolt: Oracle is cutting around 3,000 jobs while Microsoft puts about 500 employees on PIPs as companies shift budgets towards newer skills
Article Text:
India’s IT hiring landscape is undergoing a significant change.

Oracle job cuts , Microsoft PIPs in focus

IT sector workforce trends

Indian IT sector churn

Indian IT hiring: What's changing

Layoffs have headlined the global tech landscape for over a year now and the trend continues as the industry faces one its biggest disruptions in recent years. In India too the tech hiring and firing situation is evolving fast, and be it Indian IT companies or MNCs with India branches, the disruption is real.Global tech giant Microsoft has put around 500 employees in India on performance improvement plans (PIPs), while Oracle is preparing to cut roughly 3,000 jobs in the country as technology companies reorganise their workforces and redirect spending towards newer areas, according to an ET report. Experts however note that performance improvement plans need not translate into layoffs.Industry executives point out that putting employees on PIPs does not necessarily mean the company is pursuing layoffs, as such plans can also form part of normal performance management processes.Pareekh Jain, chief executive of market research firm EIIRTrend told ET that about 2% of Microsoft India’s workforce, or approximately 400-500 employees, could be affected by the company’s global PIP exercise.Jain estimated that Oracle’s latest job cuts could affect between 2,000 and 3,000 employees. Oracle employs around 30,000 people in India. The company had already eliminated about 12,000 jobs in the country during an earlier round of layoffs.In response to a query from the financial daily, a Microsoft spokesperson said the company follows a formal performance improvement plan and global voluntary separation agreement processes. Employees who fall short of the expectations associated with their roles may be offered coaching, placed on a PIP, given the option of voluntary separation, or terminated.“The share of employees globally on PIPs is a very small percentage,” the spokesperson said, adding that Microsoft does not comment on individual personnel matters or provide regional breakouts.Gaurav Vasu, chief executive of market research firm UnearthInsight, said the reported 2% figure in India should not automatically be viewed as evidence that companies are replacing layoffs with performance-based exits. “Typically, 1% to 2% of the workforce is what can be considered involuntary attrition or PIP-related attrition,” he said. “This can be due to a skill mismatch or a performance issue. So the reported 2% figure is part of a regular process. ”According to Vasu, Oracle’s restructuring is indicative of the changing skills and functions that technology companies are choosing to prioritise. “The restructuring is essentially about moving budgets from legacy sales skills to new-age skills,” he said.“In Oracle’s case, it is a combination of PIP and a shift towards new-age areas. It is an AI-led restructuring where budgets are being reallocated between legacy skills and new-age skills.”Kamal Karanth, co-founder of staffing firm Xpheno, said PIPs are “not necessarily an alternative to layoffs” and are instead intended to provide employees with an opportunity to improve their performance.He added that the effects of AI on engineering employment are expected to become increasingly apparent over the next two to three years. Junior and mid-level engineers working on lower-complexity tasks are likely to face greater exposure to this shift.India’s IT hiring landscape is undergoing a significant change, particularly for freshers, as large technology companies become more cautious about campus recruitment. Alongside selective hiring, a growing number of companies are also delaying the onboarding of fresh graduates, leaving many candidates uncertain about when they will actually begin their jobs.Earlier this year it was reported that companies such as IBM, Accenture, Oracle Financial Services Software and Cognizant have told candidates that their joining dates will depend on factors including project availability, business needs and administrative processes. As a result, some engineering graduates were left waiting for months, and in certain cases more than a year, before they can start work.Experts say hiring is increasingly being determined by specific projects and actual demand, rather than companies recruiting large numbers of freshers simply to build bench strength.The shift is part of a wider reset across the IT industry. India’s five largest IT companies reduced their combined workforce by a net 6,981 employees in FY26, after adding 12,718 employees in FY25. Meanwhile, Nasscom estimates that the industry’s overall workforce increased by only 1.35 lakh to 5.9 million in 2026.There are, however, some signs of improvement. India’s six largest IT companies added a net 5,400 employees in the first quarter of FY27, reversing the net reduction of 7,100 jobs recorded in the preceding quarter. TCS accounted for much of the increase, adding 9,000 employees net, its largest quarterly workforce addition in three years.As the traditional IT hiring model changes, Global Capability Centres (GCCs) are becoming important employers for technology talent. These offshore units of multinational companies manage functions such as technology, engineering, finance, R&D, analytics and other business operations for their global organisations.However, HR professionals do not see GCCs as a direct, like-for-like replacement for conventional campus recruitment. Their hiring is increasingly centred on specialised capabilities, including AI, data analytics, product development, cybersecurity and digital engineering, rather than large-scale recruitment of fresh graduates.
Article Summary: Microsoft has put around 500 employees in india on performance improvement plans (pips) oracle is preparing to cut roughly 3,000 jobs in the country as technology companies reorganise their workforces and redirect spending towards newer areas. Experts say pips are not necessarily an alternative to layoffs.

Article Title: India eyes drones that helicopters can launch, control and send 80km into enemy territory
Article Text:
A Black Hawk helicopter launches a loitering munition; the Indian Air Force too is seeking such weapons. (image credit: Anduril)

India’s ₹20,000 Crore Drone Push: Why India Is Betting Big on Indigenous Warfare

Helicopter-launched loitering munitions are quickly becoming the next big frontier in aerial warfare, and recent trials are showing just how far the concept has come. At Project Convergence Capstone 6, a US Army H-60M Black Hawk crew successfully executed a rocket-powered launch of the Altius-700, deploying a hunter-killer team that autonomously located a target, shared data across the formation, and carried out a strike, all without putting the helicopter crew in harm's way. It marks another meaningful step toward fielding what the US Army calls launched effects, pushing sensors and weapons deeper into contested airspace while keeping manned aircraft further back from danger.Israel, too, has been busy on this front, a private firm in has developed a modular aerial launch system that lets both utility and attack helicopters deploy its Hero-120 loitering munition. What makes the system particularly versatile is its ability to hand over control of the munition mid-flight to ground forces, enabling beyond-line-of-sight engagements and tighter coordination between air and land units. Swappable warheads mean the same platform can switch between hitting armour, soft targets, or simply conducting surveillance, all decided on the fly.India is now moving to build a similar capability of its own. The Indian Air Force is seeking Non-Line-of-Sight guided ammunition for its helicopters, aiming for a lightweight, cost-effective system with a range of 50 to 60 kilometres that can hit both armour and softer targets with real-time video feed and man-in-the-loop control, allowing crews to alter or abort a strike mid-flight if needed.Alongside this, the IAF has released a Request for Proposal for drones deployable from helicopters, expected to carry at least a 500-gram warhead over an 80 km range, and a separate Request for Information for loitering munitions launched from transport aircraft, which would need a far longer 500 km range, a 30 kg warhead, and cruising speeds of 350-400 km/h.The strategic logic here is fairly straightforward. By spreading strike and surveillance capability across helicopters, the IAF could free up its fighter fleet for other missions, a meaningful advantage given the force's ongoing squadron shortage. These air-deployable systems aren't limited to strikes either, they can just as easily be used for electronic warfare, decoy operations, or to search for targets.India isn't alone in this pursuit, the US Air Force's parallel Gremlins programme and the broader Air Launched Effects initiative both envision networked drone swarms capable of overwhelming enemy defences from range, while China, Russia and the United Kingdom are reportedly pursuing comparable concepts of their own, suggesting helicopter and transport-aircraft-launched munitions could soon become a standard fixture of modern air combat doctrine.
Article Summary: The indian air force is seeking non-line-of-sight guided ammunition for its helicopters. The iaf has released a request for proposal for drones deployable from helicopters, expected to carry at least a 500-gram warhead over an 80 km range.

Article Title: Apple added these MacBooks to its ‘obsolete list’: What it means for users
Article Text:
How Apple's vintage and obsolete system works

What it means for users

A look back at what made these models notable

Apple has officially added the 2018 Retina MacBook Air, the 13‑inch 2018 MacBook Pro (four Thunderbolt 3 ports), and the 13‑inch 2017 MacBook Pro (two Thunderbolt 3 ports) to its obsolete products list. This means that the users of the above mentioned MacBook will not be able to receive hardware repairs. All three had previously been sitting on Apple's separate "vintage" list before being moved into the more restrictive obsolete category.Apple's classification system runs on a fixed timeline. A product is added to the vintage list once five years have passed since Apple last distributed it for sale, and it graduates to obsolete status at the seven-year mark. The distinction between the two categories matters significantly for owners: vintage products can still be repaired at Apple retail stores and Apple Authorized Service Providers as long as Apple has the necessary parts on hand. Obsolete devices, by contrast, are generally no longer eligible for repair at all, and Apple stops manufacturing replacement components for them going forward.Owners of these devices should be aware of the following:* No official repairs for obsolete products like the iPad mini 4.* Limited service for vintage products like the 2017 MacBook Air, depending on parts availability.* Software updates are unlikely, which may affect app compatibility and security.* Third-party repair options may be the only alternative for maintenance.The 2018 MacBook Air held a particular significance in the product line's history — it was the first Air model to include Touch ID and a Retina display, following earlier Air models that used a lower-resolution, less vibrant non-Retina screen. That same year also marked a broader redesign for the Air line, introducing smaller bezels and a thinner, lighter overall chassis.The 2017 MacBook Pro, meanwhile, ran on Intel's Kaby Lake processors and represented a fairly minor processor-focused update with few other significant changes. The following year's 2018 refresh added True Tone display support for the first time, along with a third-generation butterfly keyboard.
Article Summary: Apple has officially added the 2018 retina macbook air, the 13‑inch 2018 macbook pro, and the 13-inch 2017 macbook pro to its obsolete products list. All three had previously been sitting on apple's separate "vintage" list before being moved into the more restrictive obsolete category.

Article Title: As Florida orders removal of Flock cameras from highways, Jacksonville Sheriff 'thanks' security camera company; calling it 'enormously valuable', but ...
Article Text:
As Florida orders removal of Flock cameras from highways, Jacksonville Sheriff 'thanks' security camera company

Florida Flock Safety cameras face removal after privacy and accuracy concerns

Other Florida sheriff's offices are also ending Flock camera use

Florida is ordering automated license plate reader cameras off its state highways, but Jacksonville Sheriff T.K. Waters has offered an unusual response to the company behind the technology. As the state moves to remove Flock Safety cameras from the Florida highway system, Waters said the technology had been an “enormously valuable” investigative tool for his department. However, he also said concerns raised by residents, along with the state's decision, meant it was time to stop using the technology across Duval County.The Florida Department of Transportation issued a memo revoking permits for automated license plate readers, or ALPRs, on roads that are part of the state highway system. The department said the cameras must be removed within 30 days. The decision comes as Flock Safety faces growing criticism over how its cameras collect and use license plate data.Flock cameras are used in thousands of communities across the US. The cameras are generally placed along roads or at intersections, where they capture license plates and other vehicle information.Police departments use the data to help investigate crimes, locate vehicles and find missing or vulnerable people.But the technology has also attracted concerns about privacy and surveillance. Critics have questioned how much information is collected, how long it is stored and who can access it.There have also been concerns about the accuracy of the cameras.An investigation by Business Insider in March identified a dozen cases in which Flock cameras misread license plates or officers failed to properly verify alerts. Those errors resulted in several cases where people who had not committed crimes were stopped or detained by police.In July, Business Insider reported that Flock cameras in Roseville, California, had misread license plates in 71% of alerts sent to police during 2023 and 2024.Residents in different parts of the US have pushed for the cameras to be removed. In some places, people have also vandalized cameras by covering them with trash bags or paint. Jacksonville sheriff says Flock cameras were valuable, but community concerns changed the decisionJacksonville is now among the Florida communities moving away from the technology. Following the Florida Department of Transportation's decision, Sheriff T.K. Waters said the Jacksonville Sheriff's Office would discontinue the use of license plate readers throughout Duval County.Waters still praised the technology's usefulness.“LPR technology has proven to be an enormously valuable investigative tool, assisting our agency in solving serious crimes and locating missing and vulnerable individuals,” Waters said.But he added that the state decision and concerns from residents had changed the situation.“However, given the decision made at the state level and the concerns expressed by members of our community, I have determined that discontinuing the use of this technology is the appropriate course of action at this time.”The decision means Jacksonville will stop using the license plate reader technology even though its sheriff says it had helped investigators.Jacksonville is not alone. Sheriff's offices in Franklin County, Liberty County and Putnam County have also said they will discontinue the use of Flock cameras following the state's decision.They are joining a growing number of communities that have ended their relationship with Flock Safety. Last week, Tempe, Arizona, announced that it would shut down its network of 33 Flock cameras. The city cited concerns about possible misuse and the need to maintain public trust.The Los Angeles Police Department also allowed its Flock contract to expire in July. Flock Safety did not respond to a request for comment on the latest developments.
Article Summary: Florida orders removal of flock safety cameras from highways. Jacksonville sheriff t.k. Waters 'thanks' security camera company. Other florida sheriff's offices are also ending flock camera use. Florida department of transportation says cameras must be removed within 30 days.

Article Title: American companies' datacenter troubles may be just getting bigger, and the reason is what has also made Europe, China, Canada and many other countries 'angry'
Article Text:
Representative Image

‘Major tech companies already taking measures’

American technology giants pouring billions into artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure may soon encounter an obstacle at home: a proposed expansion of US tariffs that may significantly elevate the cost of building data centres. According to a report by The Politico, the Trump administration is weighing a sweeping round of duties on semiconductors. Citing eight people familiar with the discussions, the report says that the plan under review will broaden import taxes beyond bare chips to include finished hardware such as servers, consumer laptops and gaming systems.Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is said to be advocating for a framework that links tariff exemptions for foreign firms to commitments to invest in domestic fabrication plants, with an additional phase-in period under review.It is noteworthy that Trump has targeted Europe, China and Canada with a series of tariffs and trade pressures that have escalated tensions between the nations. In Europe, the Trump administration has condemned tech laws and regulatory policies; Beijing, in the past, has stopped exports of rear Earth metals after Trump imposed tariffs on China and Canada recently announced retaliatory tariffs on goods, including steel and aluminium.The proposal has sparked alarm across Silicon Valley with major tech companies already said to be navigating severe shortages of high-performance chips, a situation made worse by unprecedented demand for AI data centers.While industry representatives back long-term domestic manufacturing, they emphasise that cutting-edge fabrication facilities cost billions and take years to become operational. In the interim, American cloud operators remain dependent on overseas supply chains in South Korea, Malaysia and Taiwan – which alone produces over 90% of top-tier logic chips.Industry leaders warn that taxing foreign silicon will negatively impact the primary resource fueling the compute boom, potentially forcing companies to scale down server campus investments. With TSMC projecting that its Arizona facilities will account for roughly 30% of its advanced output even after huge investments, tech leaders warn that proposed duty-free quotas will fall well short of data center demands, the report emphasised.

Article Title: FBI has a 'Public Service Announcement' for everyone on the internet: You may be targeted by ...
Article Text:
What is 'OAuth consent phishing', and what makes it dangerous

How 'OAuth Consent Phishing Works

The cyber division of Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) has released a Public Service Announcement providing insight regarding a recent campaign of malicious cyber actors targeting prominent victims through a technique known as OAuth consent phishing. According to FBI advisory, "Since late 2025, malicious cyber actors have been targeting prominent victims, their family members, and personal acquaintances by directly messaging personal accounts with malicious links leveraging a technique known as 'OAuth consent phishing'.OAuth is a commonly used authorization framework which enables websites and Web applications to request access to a user's account on another application without the user exposing their login credentials to the requesting application.OAuth consent phishing is a deceptive, sophisticated approach to access user accounts without requiring a password. It typically begins with a phishing email or direct message through a CMA and, when the user clicks the malicious link, they are redirected to a legitimate communication provider permission request screen. If the user approves the request, they unwittingly grant high-level access to a malicious application controlled by the cyber actor.From that moment, the cyber actor can act on behalf of the user, including reading and sending emails, and accessing sensitive data without having access to the user's credentials. By registering malicious applications through legitimate authorization protocols and using social engineering tactics, cyber actors can bypass both passwords and multi-factor authentication, which makes consent phishing especially dangerous.FBI says that recently observed activity includes impersonating government officials, media, and other publicly known personalities on a commercial messaging application (CMA) and soliciting the targeted individual to access a malicious link under the guise of a file sharing service through an application under the malicious actor's control. Previous phishing campaigns have also impersonated event coordinators and planners, who sent malicious links to targets under the guise of an invitation to an event and the need to verify the target's identity through a malicious application under the actor's control.OAuth is a commonly used authorization framework which enables websites and Web applications to request access to a user's account on another application without the user exposing their login credentials to the requesting application.Historically, spear phishing efforts focused on social engineering ruses with links or access to malicious credential harvesting sites or malware deployment to gain access to target accounts or devices. OAuth consent phishing provides actors with persistent access to a target's account because once permission is obtained, it can only be revoked by the victim invalidating the token in their application security settings; not by changing the password.How internet users can protect themselvesMitigation strategies include increased scrutiny of communications from unfamiliar phone numbers, accounts, or that are not part of a known contact list. Additionally, independently verify the identity of the sender and only grant authorization to trusted applications.
Article Summary: Malicious cyber actors targeting prominent victims through a technique known as oauth consent phishing. Oauth is a commonly used authorization framework which enables websites and web applications to request access to a user's account on another application. It typically begins with a phishing email or direct message through a cma.

Article Title: Larry Ellison and son David accused of 'powering some of the most destructive forces in the world'; Paramount issues rare statement
Article Text:
Upset Paramount issues statement on Mark Ruffalo

What Mark Ruffalo told his 20 million Instagram followers that made Paramount issue rare statement

American actor Mark Ruffalo has triggered a new debate in Hollywood after his comments slamming Oracle CEO Larry Ellison and his son David Ellison. In a post on Instagram, Ruffalo accused the father and son duo of "powering some of the most destructive forces in the world. " The award-winning actor re-posted an year-old video clip featuring Jewish Paramount Skydance board member Safra Catz speaking on a panel. In text accompanying the clip he told his 20 million Instagram followers it showed Catz "revelling" in a "genocide" powered by tech company Oracle. For those unaware, Catz is the former CEO of Oracle, which was co-founded by Larry Ellison, father of Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison.Responding to his post, Paramount issued a rare statement condemning Ruffalo. The company said that it is "troubled when antisemitic tropes are invoked in purported service of a business dispute.""Words like ‘genocide’ and ‘apartheid,’ applied to a corporate transaction, aren’t just wrong — they’re a bridge too far, and they cheapen the very real suffering those words are meant to describe. This doesn’t deserve a response in kind — and to be clear, we don’t tolerate prejudice of any kind, against anyone.”“This brings us to a moment to lower the temperature, not raise it. We’d rather build than further engage in such rhetoric. This simply exposes the true motivation of some who have advocated opposition to this transaction. On the other hand, our commitment to great content is matched by our commitment to acceptance – to every story, every storyteller, and no blacklists, no exceptions, for anyone.”Earlier today, Ruffalo shared a video of Oracle’s executive vice chair Safra Catz boasting about the company’s efforts to "advance the agenda for the Israeli military" by making "really profoundly scary technology" available to them. He slammed the Ellison family's ties to Israel and their role in “what we now have come to see as a genocide” in Gaza, adding: "This is the company that Larry Ellison is using to fund his son David’s Warner Bros acquisition. "The dispute traces to a social media post from the Boycott, Divestment, and Sanctions (BDS) movement. The post featured comments from Oracle Executive Vice Chair Catz describing the company’s assistance to Israel following the October 7, 2023, Hamas attack. BDS captioned the clip by accusing Oracle of being “complicit in war crimes and crimes against humanity — including apartheid and genocide against Palestinians. ”Ruffalo re-shared the post to his Instagram Story and wrote, "These ‘really profoundly scary technologies’ will most likely be merged into one of the largest media conglomerates in the world and one day used on you,” Ruffalo wrote. “Look how [Catz] revels in what we now have come to see as a genocide, which was built on an apartheid system of oppression powered by Oracle." Ruffalo further urged his followers to push back against the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger, arguing it would be “catastrophic for our film industry”In his response to Paramount's criticism post, Ruffalo reiterated that his criticism was not directed at Jewish people. He wrote, "The accusation that I am antisemitic is appalling and fundamentally dishonest. Criticizing the actions of the Israeli prime minister, a military technology contract, or the executives who supply it is not the same as criticizing Jewish people. This critical and necessary dialogue is then dishonestly framed as being anti-Israel. To be clear, my views come from my own political convictions and should never be interpreted as hostility toward Jewish people, for whom I have deep love and respect. Everything I know about acting, activism, and humanism has been profoundly shaped by the Jewish friends, colleagues, and loved ones who have been integral and family throughout every point of my life."
Article Summary: Upset paramount issues statement on mark ruffalo. Ruffalo accused the father and son duo of "powering some of the most destructive forces in the world" the actor re-posted an year-old video clip featuring jewish paramount skydance board member safra catz speaking on a panel.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Apple’s CEO John Ternus: “Build what interests you, build what excites you, but above all…”
Article Text:
Quote of the day by John Ternus

“Build what interests you,

build what excites you

, but above all else, build it in a way that aligns with your values.”

What John Ternus meant by building around your values

Ternus built his career on the engineering side of Apple

Ternus's work went far beyond how an Apple device looked

Ternus became Apple CEO in 2026

Ternus's three-part test adds a missing question to career advice

Building does not mean getting everything right

Lessons to learn from John Ternus’s quote

Let curiosity guide your direction

Choose something that keeps you engaged

Do not follow passion blindly

Keep your values involved in your decisions

Think beyond the finished result

Know what is worth your effort

Balance ambition with principles

Build something you can stand behind

John Ternus has spent much of his career working behind products that people use every day, dealing with the engineering decisions that determine how those products look, work and hold up over time. Now, as Apple’s chief executive, his words about building have a wider audience. In a 2024 commencement address at the University of Pennsylvania, Ternus told graduates to build things that interest and excite them, while making sure those things fit their values. The advice is straightforward, but the final part changes its meaning. It is not simply about finding enjoyable work or chasing an interesting idea. It asks people to think about what they are creating and whether it reflects the principles they want to stand behind. Coming from an engineer whose career has centred on designing and developing hardware, the choice of the word 'build' is particularly fitting.The quote was delivered by Ternus during his 2024 commencement speech at the University of Pennsylvania, where he had studied mechanical engineering. The first part of Ternus’s advice is about curiosity. People tend to spend a great deal of their working lives on a relatively small number of subjects, so having a genuine interest in the problem can make a difference.Excitement adds something slightly different. Being interested in a subject does not necessarily mean finding every part of the work enjoyable. Difficult projects can involve repetition, setbacks and long stretches when progress is hard to see. Ternus’s point is not that work should always be fun. It is that there should be something about the work that keeps a person engaged with it.Then comes the qualification: values come first. That shifts the quote away from simple career advice. A project can be technically impressive or personally exciting and still not be something a person wants to help create. Values provide the boundary around the other two ideas.Ternus’s own professional background makes the language of building especially appropriate.He studied mechanical engineering at the University of Pennsylvania before beginning his career at Virtual Research Systems. He joined Apple in 2001, initially working within the company’s product design organisation. Over the years, his responsibilities expanded across hardware engineering and some of Apple’s most recognisable products.Apple says Ternus became vice president of Hardware Engineering in 2013 and joined the company’s executive team in 2021. His rise was therefore closely tied to the technical side of the company rather than following a conventional route through finance or sales.Ternus eventually became senior vice president of Hardware Engineering, overseeing the teams responsible for Apple’s hardware development.That role placed him close to the practical process of turning ideas into finished products. Hardware engineering involves far more than the appearance of a device. Materials, reliability, manufacturing, durability and the interaction between different components all have to work together.The position also meant working across several product categories at once. A decision that makes sense for one device may not necessarily work for another. Engineering teams have to balance performance, size, cost, manufacturing constraints and the experience of the person using the finished product.Apple announced in April 2026 that Cook would become executive chairman and Ternus would become CEO on September 1, 2026. His appointment followed years of increasing responsibility within the company.He therefore took over after more than two decades at Apple, much of that time spent working on hardware.The transition also meant that an engineer with extensive experience in product development moved into the role responsible for the company as a whole.Ternus’s quote can be read as a simple three-question test.First, does the subject genuinely interest you?Second, is there something about the work that excites you enough to keep learning and improving?Third, does what you are building fit with your values?The third question is the one that prevents the advice from becoming another version of “follow your passion”.Interest can tell someone where to look. Excitement can help sustain attention. Values can help determine where the line should be drawn.There is also an important implication in the word “build”.A finished product is usually the visible result of many versions that never reached the public. Ideas are tested, changed, rejected and rebuilt. The same can happen with a career.Ternus’s own path at Apple was not a single leap from engineer to chief executive. He moved through different positions and took on broader responsibilities over many years.That makes the quote less about finding one perfect project and more about deciding what is worth continuing to work on. Sometimes the first version is wrong. That does not necessarily mean the entire idea has failed. It may simply need to be rebuilt.
Article Summary: John ternus gave the quote in a 2024 commencement address at the university of pennsylvania. He told graduates to build things that interest and excite them, while making sure those things fit their values. The advice is straightforward, but the final part changes its meaning.

Article Title: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 models claimed to be ‘world’s most advanced models for coding and knowledge work’
Article Text:
Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 models

Claude Fable 5.1 brings lower costs and stronger coding performance: Anthropic

New Claude model aims to help with scientific research

Claude Mythos 5.1 is restricted to approved users

Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 availability

Anthropic has launched two new AI models, Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1, with a focus on coding, research and complex knowledge work. The company says the new models can handle longer and harder tasks while also reducing costs for many users. Fable 5.1 is available to everyone, while Mythos 5.1 is limited to approved users working in areas such as cybersecurity and life sciences. The two models are essentially the same model, but come with different safety controls. Anthropic says Mythos 5.1 has more flexible safeguards for vetted researchers and security professionals. Announcing the two models, Anthropic said: “They’re the world’s most advanced models for coding and knowledge work—and their research capabilities offer an early glimpse of how AI models will contribute to scientific progress”.Anthropic says Claude Fable 5.1 will cost about 25% less than Fable 5 for typical workloads when usage is charged by tokens. For highly agentic tasks, which involve the AI working through many steps and using tools, the savings can reach about 45%.The lower cost comes mainly from a 75% cut in the price of cache reads. Cache reads allow the model to reuse information it has already processed. Anthropic says Fable 5.1 will continue to cost $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens, while cache reads will cost $0.25 per million tokens.The company also says the model performed better than its predecessor on several tests. On CursorBench 3.2.0, for example, Fable 5.1 scored 73.4%, compared with 70.5% for Fable 5 and 70% for Opus 5.Anthropic is also highlighting the research abilities of its new models. In one test, Claude Fable 5.1 created a new high-resolution elevation map of part of Venus using old radar images from NASA's Magellan mission. Anthropic says the map shows details as small as two to three kilometres, compared with 10 to 20 kilometres in the earlier map.The company also tested Claude Mythos 5.1 for protein design. Anthropic says the model created protein binders that showed strong results in laboratory testing. Across 12 targets, the model achieved a hit rate of nearly 50%, which the company says is much higher than the typical 10% to 15% rate in protein design.Mythos 5.1 was also used to optimize seven open-source biology and genomics models. Anthropic says the models ran up to 2.5 times faster, while estimated GPU costs for some genome-wide analyses fell by 30% to 60%.Anthropic is not making Mythos 5.1 generally available. The model is being offered through trusted access programs for selected cybersecurity professionals and life sciences researchers. The company says these users can access capabilities that are restricted in the standard Fable 5.1 model.For cybersecurity, Anthropic says Fable 5.1 can now help find software vulnerabilities as part of defensive security work. However, tasks such as exploit generation and penetration testing remain restricted.The company also says its updated cybersecurity safeguards produce about 60% fewer false-positive interventions than the previous safeguards.For life sciences, Anthropic has created an access program for professionals using Mythos 5.1 for research and development. The program was developed in partnership with the US government.Anthropic is also introducing Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, or EFS, for enterprise customers. The system is designed to provide privacy similar to a zero-data-retention setup while allowing Anthropic to maintain safeguards against misuse. Under EFS, customer data is stored in cloud infrastructure controlled by the customer rather than Anthropic.The feature will begin rolling out to enterprise customers in phases later this fall.Claude Fable 5.1 is available immediately across Anthropic's platforms. Developers can also access it through the Claude API, while the model is available through cloud platforms including Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure.Mythos 5.1, meanwhile, remains restricted to vetted users as Anthropic continues to balance its more advanced capabilities with safety concerns.
Article Summary: Anthropic launches claude fable 5.1 and mythos 5. 1 models. Company says the new models can handle longer and harder tasks while also reducing costs for many users. The two models are essentially the same model, but come with different safety controls. Fable is available to everyone, while mythos is limited to approved users.

Article Title: JioHotstar launches in UK, Canada and Singapore with new shows and live features
Article Text:
JioHotstar launches in UK, Canada and Singapore with new shows and live features

JioHotstar brings 160,000+ hours of Indian entertainment to international audience

JioHotstar subscription plans for UK, Canada and Singapore

JioHotstar has launched in the UK, Canada and Singapore, bringing its Indian entertainment catalogue to audiences outside India. In a press release, the company said that the “launch goes beyond taking JioHotstar’s extensive entertainment catalogue to new markets” and “brings audiences a new way to discover, watch and engage with entertainment combining 160K+ hours of content across 12+ languages and multiple genres with personalized recommendations, interactive features, flexible subscription options and a delightful product experience”.JioHotstar offers content across several categories, including television, films, regional programming, non-fiction, kids' content and anime. The platform's library includes popular shows and originals such as Criminal Justice, Special Ops, Asur, Aarya, Pritam & Pedro, Heartbeat, Kerala Crime Files and Resort.Its film catalogue includes titles such as Dhurandhar, 12th Fail, Chhichhore, Kesari Chapter 2: The Untold Story of Jallianwala Bagh, Kill, Jab We Met and Vaazha. JioHotstar said it plans to add more than 30,000 hours of fresh content every year, giving users access to a continually expanding catalogue. The platform has kicked off its international launch with a diverse line-up of entertainment that includes:New Originals & Blockbuster Premieres: A slate of originals including Ali Baba Aur Chaalis Bhoot, Prince of Mollywood, Part Timers, The Court and more alongside blockbuster movie premieres through the year. Bigg Boss , Now Interactive: The iconic reality franchise Bigg Boss returns across six languages, and for the first time, audiences across Singapore, Canada and the UK will be able to vote LIVE across every edition, giving them the power to actively participate in and influence the game in real time. While audiences in Canada and the UK will have access to the 24x7 LIVE Feed, Canada will also be able to watch Bigg Boss Hindi 7 days ahead of its TV broadcast.A New Game Show Format: Audiences in Canada and Singapore can witness the magic of Anil Kapoor hosting India Ka Top 1 Percent, a new format that tests contestants’ logic and reasoning.Content from JioStar TV Channels with Early Access: Audiences can access content from JioStar television channels, including Star Plus, Colors, Star Vijay, Asianet, Star Jalsha and Star Pravah, with Before-TV access to popular shows in Singapore and Canada, including Anupama, Yeh Rishta Kya Kehlata Hai, Seher Hone Ko Hai, Azhagae Azhagu, while audiences in the UK can watch popular shows simultaneously with their TV broadcast, alongside regional and daily entertainment.JioHotstar is also introducing new quarterly subscription plans across all three markets for the first time. The updated pricing effective 2 nd September across markets is as follows:Commenting on JioHotstar’s international expansion and vision for global streaming, Amit Malhotra, Head – International Business, JioStar, said: “Streaming has spent the last decade competing on the size of its catalogue. We believe the bigger opportunity now is to reimagine how audiences experience entertainment; not just what they watch, but how they discover, engage with and shape the experience in real time. South Asian audiences have a deep connection with Indian entertainment across languages, generations and households. At the same time, audiences globally are increasingly seeking stories and cultures beyond their own. We see an opportunity to build for this broader, underserved global audience - not simply export an Indian streaming service to new markets.”He further added, “As we expand internationally, our ambition is to show what becomes possible when scale, language, cultural diversity, personalisation and deeper audience participation are built into the streaming experience from day one.”

Article Title: Netflix unveils ‘VOID’, an AI model that can change a movie plot
Article Text:
Netflix

How Netflix VOID works







Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background. VOID goes a step further: after erasing an object from a scene, it calculates how the surrounding environment should realistically respond to its absence, and in the process it adjusts the behaviour of other elements in the frame accordingly.The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.For example, imagine this scenario: A movie director has just wrapped up a multi-million dollar action sequence where the star drives straight into a fiery, head-on collision. The cars explode, debris scatters, and the scene is a wrap.But suddenly, there is request to change the scene: The character survives and drive off into the sunset instead. This would mean costly reshoots or millions spent on computer-generated graphics.Netflix’s VOID can alter the scene and digitally erase the collision, the second vehicle, the smoke, and the flying debris. It will then generate new, realistic footage of pristine pavement, making it look as though the main character simply drove down an empty, peaceful road.The AI’s ‘magic’ lies in its grasp of real-world physics. Let us understand this by a different example. If a video shows a person jumping into a pool and splashing water onto the deck, VOID can completely erase the person. It will then intelligently alter the water and the wet concrete, leaving behind a perfectly still, undisturbed pool as if nobody had ever jumped in.“To train the model, we generate a new paired dataset of counterfactual object removals using Kubric and HUMOTO, where removing an object requires altering downstream physical interactions. During inference, a vision-language model identifies regions of the scene affected by the removed object. These regions are then used to guide a video diffusion model that generates physically consistent counterfactual outcomes,” Netflix said.“Experiments on both synthetic and real data show that our approach better preserves consistent scene dynamics after object removal compared to prior video object removal methods,” the company added.Netflix isn’t keeping this powerful tool locked behind studio doors, and made the VOID model available to the public on the AI platform Hugging Face, allowing anyone to download and use it.While there are already several video-altering tools on the market, such as Runway, DiffuEraser, and ProPainter, the Netflix team claims VOID is vastly superior, as per The Register.
Article Summary: Netflix has unveiled an ai model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background.

Article Title: AI data centers are causing 'stress' not just to tech companies, but also private insurers
Article Text:
Massive investments, growing risks



Unique challenges for data centre insurance companies





AI data centers are reportedly putting new pressure on the insurance industry. According to a CNBC report, experts warn that the rapid growth of these projects is becoming a “stress test” not just for tech companies, but also for private insurers and lenders. Consulting firm McKinsey estimates that global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030. As costs rise, tech giants are increasingly relying on private equity, private credit and debt to fund these projects. The scale of investments is creating challenges for insurers.“When you put $10 to $20 billion plus in a single location, it creates capacity issues in the marketplace,” said Tom Harper, data center leader at insurance broker Gallagher as quoted in the CNBC report.He added that the sector has been a “real stress test” over the last few years, as insurers struggle to provide coverage for such large and complex projects. While these facilities are seen as high-quality assets, Harper said insuring them has become difficult due to their size and risk concentration.Private data center deals have crossed $10 billion regularly, with some reaching as high as $40 billion. Companies including Nvidia, Microsoft and BlackRock have already taken part in large investment deals.Rajat Rana, partner at Quinn Emanuel Urquhart & Sullivan, described the scale as unprecedented. “We’re talking about trillions of dollars, and almost going back to the same cycle where there’s almost no transparency about the financing structures — the scale is astronomical,” he said. He added that the boom in AI data centers could be “the largest peacetime investment project in human history.”Experts say the way these projects are financed is adding another layer of risk. Much of the funding is happening through complex and less transparent debt structures. Rana warned that this trend feels like “deja vu,” referring to past financial cycles. He said the lack of transparency could create risks for investors, insurers and pension funds.As stated in the CNBC report, data centers offer unique challenges due to their mix of real estate and advanced technology. Insurers are now designing custom policies to manage these risks. However, challenges remain. Large facilities are often located in areas prone to extreme weather, and they store expensive equipment, sometimes even before installation.Another key concern is the mismatch between the lifespan of data centers and the hardware they use. While data centers can last decades, GPUs — the chips powering AI — typically last around seven years. Rana described this as a “GPU debt treadmill,” saying, “This is almost like a treadmill that these AI data centers are running on.”He explained that companies may need to keep raising debt to upgrade infrastructure as technology evolves.
Article Summary: Private data center deals have crossed $10 billion regularly, with some reaching as high as $40 billion. Mckinsey estimates that global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030. Tech giants are increasingly relying on private equity, private credit and debt to fund these projects.
